outline.chapter_title: From 16-bit Transformers to 1.58-bit LLMs: Motivation and Foundations
outline.description: Introduce the problem space and motivation behind 1.58-bit Large Language Models, positioning BitNet b1.58 within the evolution from full-precision LLMs and post-training quantization to purpose-built low-bit architectures.
subtopics: Compute and memory bottlenecks in LLMs: matrix multiplications, DRAM-to-SRAM transfers, and deployment costs
Energy models for digital compute: why power is the limiting factor and the gap between FP16 add/multiply vs integer addition on modern processes
Quantization landscape: post-training quantization vs training low-bit models from scratch; why PTQ is sub-optimal at very low precision
The BitNet paradigm: replacing nn.Linear with BitLinear to realize near-multiplication-free matrix multiplications
Why 1.58 bits: ternary weights {-1, 0, +1}, log2(3) ≈ 1.58, and how zero enables explicit feature filtering and stronger modeling capacity than binary
Memory and bandwidth advantages of ternary weights and low-bit activations for inference latency and throughput
LLaMA as the de facto open-source backbone and the importance of compatibility for adoption

outline.chapter_title: Design of BitNet b1.58: Architecture and Quantization
outline.description: Detail the BitNet b1.58 architecture, its quantization mechanisms, and the practical design decisions that enable strong accuracy and system efficiency while preserving LLaMA compatibility.
subtopics: BitLinear in Transformers: how BitLinear layers replace dense linear layers and interact with attention and feed-forward blocks
Absmean quantization for weights: scaling by average absolute value, RoundClip into {-1, 0, +1}, and the role of epsilon for numerical stability
Activation quantization: per-token scaling to a symmetric range without zero-point, 8-bit activations, and why this simplifies implementation
LLaMA-alike components: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary position embeddings, and bias removal to match open-source conventions
Training from scratch with ternary weights and 8-bit activations: high-level recipe and considerations (e.g., stability, calibration, scaling)
Handling non-quantized components: embeddings remaining full precision and implications for overall memory profile
Software and kernel support: integration with Hugging Face, vLLM, llama.cpp; Ladder 2-bit kernel; FasterTransformer for latency benchmarking
System-level implementation notes: integer accumulation, dequantization boundaries, and optimizing data movement

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Evaluation: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Scaling
outline.description: Present the experimental methodology and results demonstrating that BitNet b1.58 matches or exceeds full-precision LLMs on accuracy while delivering major gains in latency, memory, throughput, and energy.
subtopics: Pretraining setup for fair comparison: RedPajama 100B tokens; model sizes including 3B, 3.9B, 7B, 13B, and 70B
Language modeling metrics: validation perplexity on WikiText-2 and C4
Zero-shot end-task evaluation: ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ via lm-evaluation-harness
Break-even and beyond: matching FP16 from 3B and 3.9B BitNet b1.58 outperforming 3B FP16 with lower cost
Latency and memory scaling: speedups increasing with model size (up to 4.1x at 70B), and why embeddings’ FP16 share diminishes at scale
Energy analysis: arithmetic composition dominated by INT additions; approximately 71.4x savings in matmul operation energy on 7nm; end-to-end trends at 512 tokens
Throughput under pipeline parallelism: 70B on two A100 80GB GPUs; up to 11x batch size and 8.9x throughput increases
New scaling law and efficiency equivalences: 13B (1.58-bit) vs 3B (FP16), 30B vs 7B, 70B vs 13B in latency, memory, and energy
Token scaling with 2T training tokens: StableLM-3B recipe benchmark (Winogrande, PIQA, SciQ, LAMBADA, ARC-Easy) and superior zero-shot results
Pareto improvement: simultaneous gains in accuracy and system cost metrics across sizes

outline.chapter_title: Implications and Future Directions: Systems, Models, and Hardware for the 1-bit Era
outline.description: Explore the broader impact of 1.58-bit LLMs on model design, deployment, and hardware, and outline a roadmap for research and engineering in the 1-bit era.
subtopics: When to choose ternary LLMs: shifting the Pareto frontier for cost vs performance in real-world deployments
1.58-bit Mixture-of-Experts (MoE): shrinking memory footprint and interconnect traffic; potential to fit larger MoE on fewer devices or a single chip
Native long-context support: reducing KV-cache memory with 8-bit activations and prospects for further lossless compression
Edge and mobile: CPU-friendliness, reduced energy and memory needs, and enabling new on-device LLM applications
Hardware co-design: opportunities for accelerators optimized for integer accumulation and ternary weights; lessons from LPU-style designs
Kernel and system optimizations beyond current baselines: pathways to surpass 2-bit kernels and reduce remaining overheads
Open research challenges: training stability at extreme low bits, activation precision trade-offs, quantizing embeddings and KV caches, evaluation beyond perplexity
Practical deployment checklist: integration steps, profiling latency/memory/energy, and monitoring accuracy regressions
